🚀 Feature
Currently, autograd engine can handle a mixture of sparse and dense gradients, but to the best of my knowledge only embedding has an option to return sparse gradients. Yet sparse gradients also naturally arise in gather/indexing ops, so it would be good to have an option for those ops to return sparse gradients
Motivation

Consider label-smoothed criterion in nlp workloads. One of the formulations (the particular form is not important) is
loss = a * logprobs.mean(-1)+(1-a)*logprobs.gather(dim=-1, index=target.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
By far the biggest bottleneck for backward is dense gradient accumulation, where 2 reads and 1 write of the dense tensor(s) of batch_size x vocab_size tensors is happening, and before that dense gradient for gather was materialized, mostly consisting of zeros, whereas all that is really needed is adding sparse gradients from gather to the logprobs.grad
We had a few issues recently about nan gradients for values that don't even contribute to loss
#15506
#15131
with the root cause summarized by @t-vi #15506 (comment)
"The problem is that index select will give zero gradient for the non-selected indices.
But you then multiply by NaN when taking the log derivative.
There is no way to distinguish "0 gradient from not used" to 0 from "the gradient happens to be 0". Then you arrive at "NaN * 0". The NaN in the gradient is inserted by the derivative formula of "log" not of the indexing."
Returning sparse gradients will allow one to distinguish between "0 gradient from not used" (there will be no gradient in the sparse case) and "the gradient happens to be 0".
There's a question of how far sparse gradients should be propagated back, but as a first step, just returning sparse gradients and immediately converting them to dense/accumulating them to dense is enough to solve problem 1) and at least some varieties of problem 2). Also, it's not clear how to indicate sparse gradients for advanced indexing operations on the API level.

Pitch
Have gather and index_select and similar operations support sparse = True/False argument with the default value of False
cc @nikitaved @pearu @cpuhrsch @IvanYashchuk @carlosgmartin, @t-vi, @vishwakftw, @samedii, @mruberry

zeros_like has two overloads:
aten::zeros_like(Tensor self) -> Tensor and aten::zeros_like(Tensor self, *, int dtype, int layout, Device device) -> Tensor, but the symbolic assumes we encounter the second: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/onnx/symbolic.py#L1130
I uncovered this when i was doing some work that disabled constant propagation. The following script has the first overload of zeros_like if we're not doing constprop:
import torch, io

class ZerosLikeTest(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return x + x.new(2, 1, 5).zero_()

traced = torch.jit.trace(ZerosLikeTest(), (torch.rand(5),), _force_outplace=True)
print(traced.graph)

f = io.BytesIO()
torch.onnx.export(ZerosLikeTest(), (torch.rand(5),), f, verbose=True)

Hi! While I'm writing CUDA extension for a module, I received the following error when calling the forward function of my module: "Expected tensor's dynamic type to be Variable, not Tensor".
After bug tracing, I found that the problem is with the following line:
at::Tensor out = at::zeros({batch_size, dim1, dim2, dim3}, torch::dtype(torch::kFloat32));

If I replace the line above with:
